title: Vertex without calculus
body: $y=ax^2+bx+c$ has its turning point at $x=-\dfrac b{2a}$, value $c-\dfrac{b^2}{4a}$. Same as completing the square: $a\left(x+\dfrac b{2a}\right)^2+c-\dfrac{b^2}{4a}$.

title: Discriminant is a decision tool
body: $b^2-4ac>0$ two real roots, $=0$ repeated (tangent), $<0$ none. For "line meets curve" put them equal, make a quadratic, read the discriminant: **tangent $\Leftrightarrow\ \Delta=0$**.

title: Sum and product of roots
body: $\alpha+\beta=-\dfrac ba$, $\alpha\beta=\dfrac ca$ — find a missing coefficient from a known root: if one root is $r$ then the other is $\dfrac ca\cdot\dfrac1r$.

title: Roots difference
body: $|\alpha-\beta|=\dfrac{\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{|a|}$.

title: AC (cross) method to factorise $ax^2+bx+c$
body: find two numbers with product $ac$ and sum $b$, split the middle term, factor by grouping. Check by expanding the factors' constant terms.

title: Perfect-square test
body: $\Delta=0$ means the quadratic is $a(x+\tfrac b{2a})^2$.

title: Quadratic in disguise
body: $x^4-5x^2+4$, $2^{2x}-3\cdot2^x+2$, $x-5\sqrt x+4$, $\dfrac1{x^2}+\dfrac3x-4$: substitute $u=x^2$, $2^x$, $\sqrt x$, $\dfrac1x$.

title: Symmetric trick for "$ax^2+bx+c$ is always positive"
body: Needs $a>0$ and $\Delta<0$. Always positive $\Leftrightarrow$ both.

title: Position of roots relative to a number $k$
body: check the sign of $f(k)$ and the vertex side.

title: Maximise/minimise a quadratic expression
body: (areas, profits): it is a vertex question, so use $-\dfrac b{2a}$ not differentiation.

title: Rationalise
body: $\dfrac1{a+\sqrt b}=\dfrac{a-\sqrt b}{a^2-b}$. The denominator becomes $a^2-b$ on sight.

title: Simplify $\sqrt{n}$
body: by pulling out the largest square factor: $\sqrt{72}=6\sqrt2$. Squares to know: $4,9,16,25,36,49,64,81,100$.

title: Square of a surd sum
body: $(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^2=a+b+2\sqrt{ab}$. Reverse it to un-nest: $\sqrt{7+2\sqrt{10}}=\sqrt5+\sqrt2$ (find two numbers with sum 7 and product 10).

title: Index laws collapse a product of different bases
body: write everything in the same prime base first, then add the exponents. $\dfrac{8^x}{2^{x+1}}=2^{3x-x-1}=2^{2x-1}$.

title: Negative and fractional powers
body: $x^{-n}=\dfrac1{x^n}$, $x^{m/n}=\sqrt[n]{x^m}$. $(a/b)^{-n}=(b/a)^n$ (flip then power).

title: Quadratic inequalities by sketch
body: solve $=0$, sketch the $\cup$ or $\cap$, read the region. Above axis for $>0$.

title: Don't multiply an inequality by something that can be negative
body: Move everything to one side, factorise, sign-diagram (or sketch). For rational inequalities multiply by the **square** of the denominator ($>0$).

title: Combining
body: write each solution as intervals and intersect (and) / unite (or).

title: Midpoint of the intersection chord
body: has $x$-coordinate $\dfrac{x_1+x_2}2=-\dfrac b{2a}$ of the substituted quadratic; plug into the line for $y$. No need for individual roots.

title: Chord length
body: $=\sqrt{1+m^2}\;|x_1-x_2|=\sqrt{1+m^2}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{\Delta}}{|a|}$.

title: Factor theorem
body: $(x-a)$ is a factor $\Leftrightarrow f(a)=0$. For $(px-q)$ test $f(q/p)$. Try $\pm1,\pm2$ and factors of the constant term (divided by factors of the leading coefficient).

title: Remainder theorem
body: remainder on division by $(x-a)$ is $f(a)$; by $(px-q)$ is $f(q/p)$.

title: Synthetic division
body: (a quick, error-free long division): for root $a$, bring down the leading coefficient, multiply by $a$, add to the next, repeat. The last number is the remainder.

title: Factorise a cubic fast
body: find one root $a$ by trial, divide, then factorise the quadratic.

title: Sum of coefficients
body: $f(1)$; **alternating sum** $f(-1)$; **constant term** $f(0)$: free information.

title: Cubic root relations (beyond spec)
body: $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-\dfrac ba$, $\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=\dfrac ca$, $\alpha\beta\gamma=-\dfrac da$.

title: Move the point, not the curve
body: transform a few key points (intercepts, turning points, asymptotes) and re-sketch.

title: Sketching a cubic
body: roots and sign pattern. A **repeated factor** touches the axis; an **odd power** crosses; a **triple root** flattens as it crosses. Leading-coefficient sign gives the ends.

title: Reciprocal graphs
body: $y=\dfrac ax$: asymptotes at the axes; after transformation, asymptotes move with the shift.

title: Straight line forms
body: $y=mx+c$; $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$; two points $\dfrac{y-y_1}{y_2-y_1}=\dfrac{x-x_1}{x_2-x_1}$; $ax+by+c=0$ with gradient $-\dfrac ab$.

title: Distance
body: $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}$; **midpoint** $\left(\dfrac{x_1+x_2}2,\dfrac{y_1+y_2}2\right)$.

title: Perpendicular bisector
body: midpoint + gradient $-\dfrac1m$. Every point on it is equidistant from the two ends: set $PA^2=PB^2$ for the locus equation straight away; the squares cancel to a linear equation.

title: Distance from a point to a line
body: (beyond spec, very handy): $\dfrac{|ax_0+by_0+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$.

title: Line through the intersection of two lines
body: $L_1+\lambda L_2=0$ is **every** line through that point; choose $\lambda$ to satisfy one more condition, with no need to find the intersection.

title: Parallel line through a point
body: same $a,b$; only $c$ changes: $ax+by=ax_1+by_1$. **Perpendicular line:** swap and negate: $bx-ay=bx_1-ay_1$.

title: Collinearity
body: equal gradients, or zero area (shoelace below).

title: Intersection of two lines
body:
substitute, or use Cramer: for $a_1x+b_1y=c_1$, $a_2x+b_2y=c_2$,
$x=\dfrac{c_1b_2-c_2b_1}{a_1b_2-a_2b_1}$, $y=\dfrac{a_1c_2-a_2c_1}{a_1b_2-a_2b_1}$.

title: Triangle with a vertex at the origin
Shoelace formula
Right-angle check
body: $PQ^2+QR^2=PR^2$, or gradients multiply to $-1$.

title: Rectangle/parallelogram from three vertices
body: $D=A+C-B$ (opposite vertices have the same midpoint).

title: Kite and rhombus
body: diagonals bisect at right angles; area $=\tfrac12d_1d_2$.

title: Equation
body: $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$. **General form** $x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$ has centre $(-g,-f)$, radius $\sqrt{g^2+f^2-c}$. Read, don't complete the square.

title: Circle through three points
body: substitute each point into $x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$: three linear equations.

title: Diameter with ends $A,B$
body: $(x-x_A)(x-x_B)+(y-y_A)(y-y_B)=0$. No centre or radius needed.

title: Angle in a semicircle is $90^\circ$
body: if a triangle has a right angle at $P$, the hypotenuse is a diameter and the centre is its midpoint.

title: Perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord
body: Two chords' perpendicular bisectors meet at the centre.

title: Tangent at $(x_1,y_1)$ on $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$
body: $(x-a)(x_1-a)+(y-b)(y_1-b)=r^2$. Or gradient $=-\dfrac{x_1-a}{y_1-b}$ (perpendicular to the radius).

title: Length of tangent from external point $P$
body: $\sqrt{(\text{distance to centre})^2-r^2}=\sqrt{x_P^2+y_P^2+2gx_P+2fy_P+c}$ (substitute the point into the general form).

title: Line meets circle
body: substitute, discriminant. **Circle touches an axis:** radius $=|$centre coordinate$|$. **Touches both axes:** centre $(r,r)$ etc.

title: Two circles touch
body: distance between centres $=r_1+r_2$ (externally) or $|r_1-r_2|$ (internally).

title: Point inside/outside
body: compare distance to the centre with $r$, or substitute into $x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c$: $<0$ inside.

title: Exact values to know cold
body:
| $\theta$ | $0$ | $30^\circ$ | $45^\circ$ | $60^\circ$ | $90^\circ$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $\sin$ | $0$ | $\tfrac12$ | $\tfrac{\sqrt2}2$ | $\tfrac{\sqrt3}2$ | $1$ |
| $\cos$ | $1$ | $\tfrac{\sqrt3}2$ | $\tfrac{\sqrt2}2$ | $\tfrac12$ | $0$ |
| $\tan$ | $0$ | $\tfrac1{\sqrt3}$ | $1$ | $\sqrt3$ | — |

  Memory aid: $\sin=\dfrac{\sqrt0,\sqrt1,\sqrt2,\sqrt3,\sqrt4}{2}$ in order, and cos is the reverse.

title: CAST via the graph, not the diagram
body: $\sin(180^\circ-x)=\sin x$, $\cos(180^\circ-x)=-\cos x$, $\sin(-x)=-\sin x$, $\cos(-x)=\cos x$, $\sin(90^\circ-x)=\cos x$, $\cos(90^\circ-x)=\sin x$, $\tan(180^\circ+x)=\tan x$.

title: Pythagorean
body: $\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$ so $1+\tan^2x=\sec^2x$ and $1+\cot^2x=\operatorname{cosec}^2x$ (beyond spec).

title: Given $\sin x=\dfrac pq$, find the other ratios from a right triangle sketch
body: No calculator.

title: $\tan x=\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$
body: an equation mixing $\sin,\cos,\tan$ → divide by $\cos$ to get $\tan$, or replace $\tan$ and multiply through.

title: Quadratic in $\sin$ or $\cos$
body: $2\sin^2x+\cos x-1=0$: replace $\sin^2=1-\cos^2$, giving a quadratic in $\cos x$. Always replace the **squared** term so the equation has only one function.

title: Never divide by a trig function that can be zero
body: factorise instead (you'd lose roots).

title: Principal value then symmetries
body: $\sin\theta=k$: $\theta_0,\;180^\circ-\theta_0$ (+360° repeats); $\cos\theta=k$: $\pm\theta_0$ (+360°); $\tan\theta=k$: $\theta_0+180^\circ n$.

title: Compound angle $\sin(ax+b)=k$
body: solve for the whole bracket, **then** list all values in the *transformed* range ($ax+b$ runs over a longer interval), then back-solve. Always write the range for $ax+b$ first.

title: General solutions (radians)
body: $\sin\theta=\sin\alpha\Rightarrow\theta=\alpha+2\pi n$ or $\pi-\alpha+2\pi n$; $\cos\theta=\cos\alpha\Rightarrow\theta=\pm\alpha+2\pi n$; $\tan\theta=\tan\alpha\Rightarrow\theta=\alpha+\pi n$.

title: Check count
body: over one full circle, $\sin$/$\cos$ give 2 solutions per value in $(-1,1)$ and $\tan$ gives 2 solutions. Count them against the graph sketch.

title: Sine rule
body: $\dfrac a{\sin A}=\dfrac b{\sin B}=\dfrac c{\sin C}$ (= $2R$, diameter of the circumcircle). **Ambiguous case:** given $a,b,A$ with $a<b$ there can be two triangles ($B$ and $180^\circ-B$).

title: Cosine rule
body: $a^2=b^2+c^2-2bc\cos A$; **rearranged** $\cos A=\dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc}$. Quick test for the type of angle: if $a^2>b^2+c^2$ then $A$ is obtuse.

title: Area
body: $\tfrac12ab\sin C$. **Heron (beyond spec):** $\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}$, $s=\tfrac{a+b+c}2$.

title: Radians (when P1 reaches them)
body: arc $s=r\theta$, sector $\tfrac12r^2\theta$, **segment** $\tfrac12r^2(\theta-\sin\theta)$, chord $2r\sin\tfrac\theta2$.

title: Small-angle approximations (beyond spec)
body: $\sin\theta\approx\theta$, $\tan\theta\approx\theta$, $\cos\theta\approx1-\tfrac{\theta^2}2$.

title: Power rule $\dfrac d{dx}x^n=nx^{n-1}$ after rewriting
body: Rewrite roots, reciprocals and quotients with a single-term denominator first: $\dfrac{x^2+3}{\sqrt x}=x^{3/2}+3x^{-1/2}$.

title: Expand before differentiating
body: unless it is a power of a bracket. For brackets raised to powers use the **chain rule**: $\dfrac d{dx}(ax+b)^n=na(ax+b)^{n-1}$ (beyond spec) — differentiate the bracket's inside last as a constant factor.

title: Tangent and normal
body: Tangent gradient $m=f'(x_1)$, normal $-\dfrac1m$; **equation $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$.** For a normal passing through a named point, substitute straight in.

title: Stationary points
body: $f'(x)=0$. **Nature by $f''$:** $>0$ min, $<0$ max, $=0$ inconclusive (use sign change). For a quadratic, use the vertex (§1).

title: Increasing/decreasing
body: a sign diagram of $f'(x)$. For "increasing for all $x$" a quadratic $f'$ needs $a>0$, $\Delta<0$.

title: Optimisation recipe
body: (1) one variable by using the constraint; (2) formula for the quantity; (3) $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0$; (4) test; (5) answer in context with units. **Look for the constraint that removes a variable first.**

title: Fixed perimeter rectangle ⇒ square maximises area; fixed area ⇒ square minimises perimeter
Closed cylinder
body: volume $V$ fixed, minimise surface area: optimum at $h=2r$ (height = diameter). Open top: $h=r$.

title: AM–GM (beyond spec)
body: for $a,b>0$, $\dfrac{a+b}2\ge\sqrt{ab}$ with equality at $a=b$. So $x+\dfrac kx\ge2\sqrt k$ with minimum at $x=\sqrt k$ — no calculus.

title: Gradient of a chord and the derivative
body: $\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}h\to f'(x)$ (first principles): for $x^n$ expand by the binomial theorem and keep the $h^1$ term.

title: Rates
body: $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=\dfrac{dy}{dx}\times\dfrac{dx}{dt}$.

title: Power rule
body: $\int x^n\,dx=\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}+c$ ($n\ne-1$); **always rewrite first** and **never forget $+c$** for indefinite integrals.

title: Linear bracket (beyond spec)
body: $\int(ax+b)^n\,dx=\dfrac{(ax+b)^{n+1}}{a(n+1)}+c$.

title: Definite integral workflow
body: integrate, substitute top, substitute bottom, subtract. Keep brackets round negative values.

title: Area between curve and $x$-axis
body: split at roots; areas below the axis count positive (take the absolute value of that part).

title: Area between two curves
body: $\int(\text{upper}-\text{lower})\,dx$ between intersection $x$-values. Sketch first: curves can swap order.

title: The one-sixth formula (parabola and chord)
body:
The area between $y=ax^2+bx+c$ and a straight line meeting it at $x=\alpha$ and $x=\beta$ is
$$A=\frac{|a|\,(\beta-\alpha)^3}{6}.$$
Two parabolas with leading coefficients $a_1,a_2$ use $a=a_1-a_2$. Check: $y=x^2$ and $y=x$: $\alpha=0,\beta=1$, $A=\tfrac16$, and $\int_0^1(x-x^2)dx=\tfrac16$ ✓. This works with **no integration** and applies to "area bounded by a parabola and a line".

title: Cubic and its tangent
body: If the tangent to $y=a(x-\alpha)^2(x-\beta)+(\text{line})$ at $x=\alpha$ meets the cubic again at $x=\beta$, the enclosed area is $\dfrac{|a|(\beta-\alpha)^4}{12}$ (the gap between cubic and tangent is $a(x-\alpha)^2(x-\beta)$).

title: Trapezium rule
body: $\tfrac h2\left[y_0+y_n+2(y_1+\dots+y_{n-1})\right]$. A curve bending upwards ($f''>0$) ⇒ trapezia **overestimate**; bending downwards ($f''<0$) ⇒ underestimate.

title: Area under $y=x^2$ from $0$ to $a$
body: is $\tfrac{a^3}3$: area of **a triangle-like ratio** — the area under $x^n$ from 0 to $a$ is $\dfrac{a^{n+1}}{n+1}=\dfrac1{n+1}\times$ the bounding rectangle. So the region between the curve and the $y$-axis (to the same height) is $\dfrac n{n+1}$ of the rectangle.

title: Finding the constant
body: substitute the given point into the integrated equation immediately.

title: Even/odd symmetry
body: $\int_{-a}^a f=2\int_0^af$ for even $f$, $=0$ for odd $f$.

title: Algebra
body: substitute a simple number ($x=1,2$) into your final and starting expressions; they must agree.

title: Trig solutions
body: sub one back in; count against the number of intersections on a sketch.

title: Differentiation
body: differentiate numerically at one point with a tiny step $h$ if unsure.

title: Integration
body: differentiate your answer; it must give the integrand.

title: Geometry
body: check distances and gradients with a rough scale sketch.

title: Quote the formula before the numbers
body: When a question needs a learned formula, write the symbolic equation first, then a separate substitution line; this makes a wrong sign or misplaced value visible and can preserve a method mark. Check that each substituted quantity occupies the same position as its symbol in the first line.

title: Keep exact values until the last line
body: When the question asks for an exact answer or uses surds or $\pi$, carry fractions and radicals through the calculation instead of reusing rounded display values. Check the final form against the instruction: a decimal is not an exact surd answer.

title: Show a mathematical step when a calculator solves it
body: For a calculator-found quadratic root or numerical answer, write the equation you solved and the substitution or factorisation that connects it to the question. Check by putting the reported root into the original equation; an unsupported calculator output may not show the method the mark scheme asks for.

title: Label the requested object and units
body: On a multi-part geometry or calculus question, finish with $x=\cdots$, $A=\cdots\ \mathrm{cm}^2$, or the requested line equation rather than an unlabelled intermediate number. Check dimensions: a length scales as $L$, an area as $L^2$, and a volume as $L^3$.
